A SuperTokens core 5xx (typically the managed core's front proxy answering 502 on `POST /recipe/session/verify`) or an unreachable core during a session check no longer surfaces as a `500 internal_error` with a Bugsink event. The SDK call is retried once after a short wait, and if it fails again the request answers a retryable `503 {"code": "auth_upstream_unavailable", ...}`; each failure is counted by the new `supertokens_core_unavailable` metric (tagged by caller and upstream status) instead of being reported to Bugsink. A core 4xx still takes the unexpected-exception path.

The handling covers every SDK call a request's authentication depends on: Bearer-token session verification (including the stateless read path, which the SDK still routes through the core for the first access token after a refresh), the browser-session cookie resolution behind the hosted accounts pages and the web chrome, the live account-email lookup, `POST /auth/session/revoke-current`, the revocation of an over-max-age browser session (which still answers 401, not 500, when the core fails the revoke), the entitlements backfill's account-age lookup, and the desktop's verification poll (`POST /auth/email/send-verification`, `POST /auth/email/is-verified`). The verification-email send itself (`POST /auth/email/send-verification`) answers the same 503 on a core outage, and the best-effort sends (the remote-workspace gate and the share broker) treat one like any other failed send: the structured `email_not_verified` refusal still goes out, with `sent: false`.
